original_value: In the case of autonomous orchard navigation, researchers have developed algorithms that utilize features, such as trunks, canopies, and sky in orchards, but there are still various difficulties in recognizing free space for autonomous navigation in a changing agricultural environment. In this study, we applied the Naive Bayesian classification to detect the boundary between the trunk and the ground and propose an algorithm to determine the center line of free space. The naïve Bayesian classification requires a small number of samples for training and a simple training process. In addition, it was able to effectively classify tree trunk’s points and noise points of the orchard, which are problematic in vision-based processing, and noise caused by small branches, soil, weeds, and tree shadows on the ground. The performance of the proposed algorithm was investigated using 229 sample images obtained from an image acquisition system with a Complementary Metal Oxide Semiconductor (CMOS) Image Sensor (CIS) camera. The center line detected by the unaided-eye manual decision and the results extracted by the proposed algorithm were compared and for several parameters. In all compared parameters, extracted center line was more stable than the manual center line results.

result.paraphrase: For autonomous orchard navigation, prior research has developed algorithms that use orchard features such as trunks, canopies, and sky, yet identifying free space remains difficult in the changing agricultural environment. In this study, we used Naive Bayesian classification to detect the trunk-ground boundary and propose an algorithm for determining the center line of free space. The naïve Bayesian approach needs only a small number of training samples and has a simple training procedure. It also effectively classified tree-trunk points and noise points in the orchard, as well as noise from small branches, soil, weeds, and tree shadows on the ground, all of which are problematic for vision-based processing. The proposed algorithm was evaluated with 229 sample images collected by an image acquisition system using a Complementary Metal Oxide Semiconductor (CMOS) Image Sensor (CIS) camera. The manually determined center line by unaided-eye decision and the center line extracted by the proposed algorithm were compared across several parameters. In every parameter compared, the extracted center line was more stable than the manual center line results.
